# ops/apps-host — control plane for the apps generated by assistants

These two files run on a separate machine, the **apps host**, not on the web service.

| file        | path on the host              | what it is                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ctl.py`    | `/opt/brambs-ctl/ctl.py`     | control plane. Receives **one JSON on stdin** and returns **one JSON line on stdout**. Called over SSH by `web/hosting.mjs`.      |
| `router.py` | `/opt/brambs-router/router.py` | scale-to-zero router on `127.0.0.1:9081` (behind Caddy:443, behind the ALB). Wakes the container on demand and sleeps on idle. |

Stdlib only in both — no `pip install` on the host.

## How it gets there

**Git is the only source of truth. Nobody edits a file directly on the host.**

Two scripts, run from a machine that has the control-channel key
(`APPS_HOST_SSH`/`APPS_HOST_KEY` in the environment or in the `.env` of the
folder they are called from, the same channel `web/appshost.mjs` uses to call
`ctl.py`). Both scripts publish/compare the `router.py` and `ctl.py` sitting
next to them, i.e. whatever is installed (in this repository or in the core
package):

| script | what it does |
| ------ | --------- |
| `check-drift.sh [--marca F] [--carimbo V]` | read-only. Compares installed vs. host and exits 1 if they diverge. |
| `deploy.sh [--aplicar] [--marca F] [--carimbo V]` | publishes. Dry-run by default. |

```bash
ops/apps-host/check-drift.sh            # does what's live match what's installed?
ops/apps-host/deploy.sh                 # dry run: what would change
ops/apps-host/deploy.sh --aplicar       # publishes for real
```

`deploy.sh` runs `test_auth.py` **before** sending any byte, makes a backup
(`.bak.<epoch>`), uploads, checks the md5 of what arrived, compiles with
`py_compile`, runs `test_auth.py` again **against the files that remain in
use**, restarts `brambs-router` only if it changed (`ctl.py` is one-shot per
call, no restart needed), stamps the version (`--carimbo`, defaults to the
commit of the folder it was called from) into
`/opt/brambs-router/.deployed-sha`, and **restores the backup if any step
fails**.

Only `router.py` and `ctl.py` go through this path.

Preferred order when the change touches the access gate: **`router.py`
first** (`deploy.sh` already does it in this order). The router is what
validates the password; if the new `ctl.py` writes `auth` entries to the
registry before the router knows how to check them, those apps are left open
in the meantime. The reverse order is safe (new router + old registry = no
app has `auth`, everything behaves as before).

This stopped being a silent window: `ctl.py` returns `private: true/false`
and the harness **only claims it locked the app if the host confirms it**. A
new platform against an old host publishes the app open and tells the
assistant to warn the user, instead of promising a password that doesn't
exist.

**Which version is live:** `cat /opt/brambs-router/.deployed-sha` on the
host, or `check-drift.sh` from here. Don't trust an md5 written by hand in
documentation.

## Configuration

The defaults below apply when nothing is configured.

| what | where | default |
| ----- | ---- | ------ |
| apps domain | `APPS_DOMAIN` in the backend's `.env`. `web/appshost.mjs` sends `dominio` in every JSON; `ctl.py` uses it to build the link returned by `publish`, the `Host` of the smoke test, and the commit email. Without `dominio` in the JSON (old backend), `APPS_CTL_PATH`'s `ctl.py` falls back to the `APPS_DOMAIN` of its own environment, which `sudo` usually clears. | the brand's site host; without a valid domain, `localhost` |
| `ctl.py` path | `APPS_CTL_PATH` in the backend's `.env` | `/opt/brambs-ctl/ctl.py`, where `deploy.sh` installs it |
| host brand (name, site, logo and badge text; the name is also the author of commits with no person behind them) | `marca.json` next to `deploy.sh` or the file passed in `--marca` (`{"nome", "site", "logo", "selo", "selo_aria"}`, all optional), which `deploy.sh` installs at `/opt/brambs-router/marca.json` and restarts the router; `BRAMBS_SITE_URL` and `BRAMBS_LOGO_URL` in the unit's environment override it | `Brambit`, `http://localhost:8080/`, `<site>/logo.svg` and "Made with Brambit" |
| router paths | `BRAMBS_REGISTRY`, `BRAMBS_INTERNAL_KEY_FILE`, `BRAMBS_USERS`, `BRAMBS_HOME`, `BRAMBS_LOG_DIR` in the unit's environment | `/opt/brambs-router/...`, `/opt/brambs-home`, `/var/log/brambs` |

The router does not depend on the domain: the label comes from the first
segment of `Host`. `ctl.py`'s paths are fixed (`/opt/brambs-*`) and must
match the router's.

## Contracts you can't break on your own

- **`/opt/brambs-router/apps.json`** is read by the router **on every
  request** (`load_registry`). Editing the registry takes effect
  immediately, no restart — that's why `set_auth` locks and unlocks a URL
  without republishing the app.
- **`/opt/brambs-router/internal.key`** (0600) is the secret shared between
  `ctl.py` and `router.py`. It's what lets `ctl`'s internal smoke test pass
  through the gate without a user password (an IP allow-list doesn't work:
  Caddy proxies from 127.0.0.1, same as everyone else). Both create the file
  with `O_EXCL` if it doesn't exist, so deploy order doesn't matter for it.
  Deleting this file breaks the publish smoke test, not user access.
- **`/app/data`** is the app's runtime data directory. It stays **outside**
  publish, snapshot and git — on purpose: user data doesn't travel in
  replication or come back in a rollback. Consequence: `delete` destroys this
  directory and **there is no backup**. That's why `apagar_sistema` in the
  harness goes through `inventory` first and asks for written confirmation.
- the gate's `hash` is `sha256(salt:password)`. This works because the
  password is generated by us, with high entropy, and the router checks it
  on every request. **If we ever accept a user-chosen password, this has to
  become pbkdf2/scrypt.**
